label: late absolute position (t=6-9) at end of original phase / <DEL>, favoring y,3,e,u,2,g,t
explanation: Fires only at absolute steps t=5..10 (almost all t=6..9) in the original and delimiter phases, so effectively only in long sequences (L>=7; 70% of mass from L=9). Essentially never fires at t<=4 or in the copy phase (13 of 12660 activations, all at the step right after <DEL>). (phase<=1)&(t>=6) covers 99.8% of activations but has only 7.6% precision. Within that window, which token is input matters a lot: y, 3, e, u (and to a lesser extent 2, g, t) carry the most activation, and the largest activations come from runs of these at t=7-8 followed by <DEL>. About 35% of the mass lands on <DEL>, mostly when the step before was active, so it looks like activation carried over from earlier steps. The recorded predicate (late step and favored token, or <DEL> right after a favored token) gets dev F1 0.39 with mass recall 0.62. Most steps in the window do not fire, and the precise token or history rule was not pinned down.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=7: y, 3, e, u; t=6: y, 3, e, u; t=8: y, 3, e, u) and the first original token (most: a, i, m, d, x, o; least: j, k, z, 2); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, L=9 & t=7, t=7.
